lesson.child_mission: A food web connects overlapping food chains when animals eat more than one food or are eaten by more than one predator.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Why is a food web often a better model of a real habitat than a single chain?

FEEDBACK
Real animals usually have more than one food or predator link; webs show those overlaps.

WATCH FOR
Drawing a web with no producers leaves consumers with nothing to start from.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Build a food web with at least eight organisms and twelve arrows. Trace two different chains inside the web and write what happens if one producer declines.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: A food web connects overlapping food chains when animals eat more than one food or are eaten by more than one predator.
materials: Optional: safe everyday objects for observation
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Build a food web with at least eight organisms and twelve arrows. Trace two different chains inside the web and write what happens if one producer declines. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Real animals usually have more than one food or predator link; webs show those overlaps. Reasoning: I used food web by attending to link rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Drawing a web with no producers leaves consumers with nothing to start from. Correction: Real animals usually have more than one food or predator link; webs show those overlaps. Why: the correction restores accurate use of food web.

Parent: Likely misconception: Drawing a web with no producers leaves consumers with nothing to start from. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses food web. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about food web, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Require a new example, named observations and a claim–evidence link. / Require misconception + corrected claim + evidence reason..

teach_steps.explain:
A food web connects overlapping food chains when animals eat more than one food or are eaten by more than one predator.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
